title: Lovable deleted most of its agent loop, then put the checks back
friendlyTitle: Lovable removed most of its free-running agent code
summary: Anton Osika writes that open-ended agents got stuck, so the team deleted almost all of that code and returned to one request and a predictable chain of tools. Short notes about recurring mistakes, retrieved into context, worked better for them than the fine-tuned models they had planned. The company says users have created more than 70 million projects.
friendlySummary: Lovable's founder says open-ended agents got stuck. The team deleted most of that code and went back to one request and a fixed set of steps. Short notes about common mistakes worked better than training a new model.
whyItMatters: More freedom for the model made the product less dependable. The practical pattern is a short instruction loaded only when it applies, plus a fast way to see the error. The open problems he names are still the hard ones: production changes, trust, and a stack that can be forked and checked.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Giving the model more freedom made the product less reliable. A short note, loaded only when it is needed, plus a fast way to see the error, was the useful change.
